title: A Choir for the Thorn
premise: Isandro Joubert has spent her life carving bones into instruments that let the valley's dead speak, hidden in a land where magic cannot cross the border. When a mute child arrives speaking the tongue of Vessarion—a kingdom erased from every map and memory—Isandro realizes the girl is the last living heir, hunted by those who unmade her country. To save her, Isandro must use her bone-choir to reconstruct the vanished kingdom's door from the memories of its dead, though each song costs her more of her own past. In the climax she trades her final memories of the valley itself to open the door, sending the child through to safety while remaining behind as a stranger to her own life. The book ends with Isandro beginning again: a woman with no history, teaching herself the names of things, while somewhere beyond the border a new country takes root.
about_author: Rosalind Sandoval is a former archivist of endangered languages who now writes fantasy about what survives when nations do not. She lives near a river valley that appears on no map older than a century.

chapters.title: The Bone That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. In the magicless valley, Isandro carves a femur into a flute for a grieving widow, establishing her gift and her careful invisibility. A child arrives at dusk, silent, drawing spirals in ash—the script of Vessarion, which only the dead have spoken to Isandro before. The emotional beat is unease blooming into recognition: isolation has ended, and something has followed the girl to the border.

chapters.title: A Country Made of Voices
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The hunters reach the valley's edge but cannot enter; they wait, patient as winter. Isandro interrogates her bone-choir of Vessarion's dead, learning the child is Princess Aurel, sole survivor of an erasure ritual—and that the door out exists only in memory. Rising dread: each testimony reveals the ritual's cost, and that the hunters can starve out anyone who shelters the heir.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Keep
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Isandro and Aurel. As food runs short, Aurel begins speaking, teaching Isandro the old tongue, and the two bond over shared orphanhood. The hunters offer a bargain: the girl for the valley's safety. Climax builds as Isandro realizes the door requires a singer who remembers Vessarion fully—and decides it must be built from her own memories instead. Emotional beat: love making sacrifice thinkable.

chapters.title: The Last Song of Vessarion
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. At the border stone, Isandro plays the completed choir, feeding it her memories one by one—her mother, her craft, the valley itself—until the door opens and Aurel passes through whole. The hunters scatter as the erased kingdom flickers back into being beyond. Resolution: memoryless Isandro wakes among strangers who call her friend, and begins, gently, to learn her own name again.
